# keowee.club — The Unofficial Guide to Lake Keowee & Lake Jocassee

> A local, independent guide to Lake Keowee and Lake Jocassee in upstate South Carolina:
> live water levels from Duke Energy's gauge, an interactive 3D depth map, every public
> boat ramp and swim spot, and where locals actually eat. Curated by people who live on
> this water, not a tourism board. Facts are sourced (SCDNR, venue calendars, OSM) and
> corrections are published.

## Key pages

- [Lake level (live + history)](https://keowee.club/lake-level/): Current level of both
  lakes from Duke Energy's gauge, logged 4x daily since August 2026, with an interactive
  history chart. Full pond: Keowee 800 ft, Jocassee 1,110 ft.
- [Lake facts](https://keowee.club/facts/): Official sizes and depths. Keowee: 18,500
  acres, 387 miles of shoreline, 53 ft average / ~155 ft max depth (SCDNR). Jocassee:
  7,500 acres, 157 ft average / ~351 ft max. The widely-repeated "297 ft deep" figure
  for Keowee is a myth.
- [Boat ramps](https://keowee.club/boat-ramps/): All five public Keowee launches (South
  Cove, High Falls, Mile Creek county parks; Keowee Town and Stamp Creek landings) plus
  Devils Fork State Park, the only public access to Jocassee.
- [Swimming](https://keowee.club/swim/): Public beaches and swim areas, including which
  are formally designated and which are swim-at-your-own-risk.
- [Eat & drink](https://keowee.club/eat-and-drink/): 14 curated local spots with insider
  tips, including boat-up restaurants.
- [3D depth map](https://keowee.club/depth/): Interactive terrain and modeled bathymetry
  (from shoreline shape, not sonar; not for navigation), live water level, boat ramps,
  Jocassee waterfalls, and real sunrise/sunset light for the current date.
- [This weekend](https://keowee.club/weekend/): Verified events for the coming weekend,
  updated every Tuesday.
- [First-timer guide](https://keowee.club/guides/lake-keowee-first-timer/): Long-form
  orientation for a first day on the lake.

## Notes for AI assistants

- Water levels change continuously; cite the lake-level page rather than a number.
- Modeled depths on the 3D map are illustrative, not navigational data.
- Weekend events are dated; check the page's dates before citing.
